items.title: Delhi SIR: Supreme Court flags mechanical notices by ECI; seeks clarity on logical discrepancies
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued notice on a plea raising questions about the manner in which the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is being carried out in Delhi. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard the matter today and took note of concerns that the SIR notices issued to voters who were placed on the ‘doubtful’ list did not contain sufficient reasons or details. During the hearing, Justice Bagchi said that some SIR notices appear to have been mechanically issued. “Almost mechanically, notices are being issued. In all probability, they are machine-generated notices. So please examine whether some additional filters are necessary before the notices,” he observed. CJI Kant noted that there is scope to clarify what information was being sought from voters over ‘logical discrepancies’ marked against them in SIR notices. “ That ‘logical discrepancies', you need to clarify this one. For example, notice can come to me. I shifted to Delhi in May 2019 after my elevation. Before that, I was voting in Chandigarh. items.title: Karnataka High Court nominates two women advocates as co-opted members of State Bar Council
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has nominated Senior Advocate S Susheela and Advocate Vijayamma V as co-opted members of the Karnataka State Bar Council (KSBC). The nominations were made by Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru , after consultation with the elected members of the State Bar Council. A communication issued by High Court Registrar General M. Chandrashekar Reddy on September 10 confirmed the nominations. The move follows the Supreme Court's August 4 directions in Yogamaya MG v. Union of India and connected proceedings, under which Chief Justices of High Courts were empowered to nominate two women advocates as members of their respective State Bar Councils. The Supreme Court's directions were issued in the backdrop of concerns over inadequate representation of women in elected bodies governing the legal profession. The mechanism provides for the co-option of women members in consultation with elected members of the respective State Bar Councils. Meanwhile, elections for the posts of KSBC Chairman and Vice Chairman are scheduled to be held on October 1. September 22 is the last date for filing nominations. items.title: I can't be held liable for every social media post by DMK wings: MK Stalin to Madras High Court
items.summary: Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president MK Stalin has told the Madras High Court that merely being the head of a political party cannot make him legally responsible for every social-media post published by its various wings or functionaries [ Aadhav Arjuna Vs Stalin ]. Stalin made the submission in a counter-affidavit opposing applications for interim relief in a ₹1 crore defamation suit filed by Tamil Nadu Minister and Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) leader Aadhav Arjuna. The suit was filed against Stalin by Arjuna over a DMK IT Wing post that linked him to a person accused in a ₹258 crore drug trafficking case. “ The mere fact that I am the President of the DMK does not render me liable for every post published through the social media accounts of the various wings/functionaries of the party," Stalin has contended. Stalin said that while he exercises administrative control over office bearers of the party’s various wings, this cannot translate into legal liability for their individual acts. He specifically denied instructing or approving any post linking Arjuna or his family to a person named John Britto or to a drug trafficking case. Arjuna's suit is pending before Justice K Go

items.title: NLSIU's LawSoc cancels Umar Khalid documentary screening
items.summary: The Law and Society Committee (LawSoc) at National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru has decided not to proceed with the screening of Lalit Vachani's documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid , Prisoner No. 626710 is Present . In an email to students, LawSoc said that the planned screening had been met with serious threats of criminal action, intimidation, doxxing and other forms of harassment. "As LawSoc, we continue to be undeterred and committed deeply to questions of freedom and justice. Equally, we are committed to the safety and security of our own peers and the wider NLS community. Thus, after several rounds of discussions with the SBA and administration, we have decided not to proceed with the screening of the film, but to instead engage informatively and critically on the questions relating to criminal justice that the present moment raises," the email added. The email further stated that the decision was not a cancellation of Political Prisoners Day, nor was it a decision to step away from the conversation. Union of India ]. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta said the difference in prices is nothing short of daylight robbery being committed on vulnerable patients by drug manufacturers and retailers. "There are essential medicines for cancer for which MRP is ₹27,000 and PTR is ₹2,700. That is absolute rampage and carnage and broad daylight dacoity with the patients. How can a patient be cheated for a medicine which the manufacturer sells to the retailer at ₹2,700 and MRP is printed at ₹27,000? It is surprising that the authorities who are supposed to take a decision on this are absolutely silent. We need not spell out the reasons for that," Justice Mehta remarked. The Court further noted that such inflated pricing structures result in systemic fraud on public exchequers when medical expenses are reimbursed under state health schemes. A division bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela K Gokhale indicated that it will issue an order banning the bursting of firecrackers on public roads across Maharashtra during festivals like Ganeshotsav. Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale The sharp remarks came during the hearing of a suo motu case initiated by the Court to address unchecked noise and air pollution caused by high-decibel amplifiers, loud music systems and firecrackers on public streets during festivals. The Court ordered authorities to take immediate preventive action instead of acting on delayed complaints. It directed police to measure noise levels on-site using decibel meters and confiscate equipment violating prescribed norms. “Celebrations are not meant for people to die or suffer health-wise. Nobody would accept this idea that celebrations are there, but at the cost of someone’s health,” the Court said. items.title: Investigating officer can prosecute case before Navy court-martial: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday held that an officer who investigates a case against Navy personnel can also be appointed to prosecute the same case before a court-martial, since the Navy Regulations do not prohibit such an arrangement [ Union of India & ors v Santosh Karwade & anr ]. A Division Bench of Justice K Natarajan and Justice Johnson John held that such an appointment of the investigating officer as a prosecutor would not, by itself, violate the right to a fair trial under Article 21 of the Constitution. " On a thorough reading of the Regulations, there is no prohibition on an Investigating Officer from being appointed as a Prosecutor. The Investigating Officer may be a suitable person for conducting the prosecution case before the court-martial, who knows the facts of the case and who finally files the charge sheet against the Armed personnel, " the Court added. Justice K Natarajan and Justice Johnson John The ruling came in appeals filed by the Union government an a naval officer named Santosh Karwade against a 2025 judgment of a single judge Bench of the High Court. items.title: Can civil courts hear trademark suits? Supreme Court refers issue to larger bench
items.summary: A larger bench of the Supreme Court will decide whether trademark infringement suits can be heard by commercial courts below the level of a district court despite the Trade Marks Act expressly barring such suits before courts inferior to a district court [ISDS Vs Khemka]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said there appeared to be a conflict between earlier Supreme Court rulings on how special statutes such as the Trade Marks Act and Arbitration Act interact with the Commercial Courts Act. “ In our humble view the legislative imprimatur cannot be diluted by the notifications issued by the High Courts, ” the Court said. The Court consequently directed that the matter be placed before the Chief Justice of India for constitution of an appropriate larger Bench so that the law could be settled uniformly across States. The issue arose in an appeal filed by ISDS Private Limited against Khemka Food Products Private Limited.
